name: Finite-range harmonic engineering to cancel residual cubic dispersion
source_anchor: Eisenberg2002 Section3.3 PDFp43 proposed arbitrary periodic diffraction synthesis; our specific static two-harmonic implementation is an inference, not the author claim.
question: At fixed total positive hopping budget, how much shape-preserving propagation distance can one gain by cancelling the cubic term, and how accurately must the extra coupling be set?
analytic_prediction: At q0=pi/2, epsilon second and fourth derivatives vanish by odd-harmonic parity; epsilon third derivative=-J1+27J3=0. The leading non-linear phase is fifth order, epsilon fifth derivative=-8J1. Expected narrow-spectrum lifetime scaling sigma^5 versus sigma^3 for the NN baseline.
fair_comparison: Same initial probability RMS width and normalization
Same total positive coupling budget J1+J3=J
Compare at matched mean propagation distance as well as time, since mean speed changes
Use full exact dispersions, not truncated differential equations, for demo data

minimal_parameter_grid.example_noise_scope: Coupling calibration error only; no separate disorder/dephasing claim

metrics: Fidelity to each initial state translated at its own spectrum-weighted mean velocity
First F=0.9 crossing time and corresponding distance
negative_control: An equally budgeted positive J3 not at 1/27 should retain cubic residual and asymptotic sigma^3 behavior. Any gain due only to slower mean speed fails the matched-distance criterion.
failure_criterion: Do not call this promising for implementation if the matched-distance gain disappears under modest calibration error or if the required hopping hierarchy cannot be generated in a specified physical platform.
demo: Three synchronized probability-envelope panels in comoving coordinates: nearest neighbor, tuned two-harmonic band, and mistuned band. Fixed probability color scale. Plot distance-resolved fidelity beside them.
limits: This tests a specified toy Hamiltonian and known band-engineering logic. It does not establish a new physical mechanism or a realizable magnetic material. Exact whole-band linearity is neither claimed nor needed.
